pick.headline: NATO adopts the double-track decision on Euromissiles
pick.summary: On December 12, 1979, NATO ministers in Brussels decided to deploy US Pershing II and cruise missiles in Western Europe from 1983, while offering arms control talks on intermediate-range missiles.
pick.significance: The decision answered the Soviet SS-20 and set off the Euromissile crisis of the early 1980s.
pick.fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of December 12, 1979, carried a Warsaw Pact foreign minister warning that a NATO decision in Brussels to deploy US medium-range missiles would upset the European balance and fuel a new arms race.

alternates.headline: Russia votes on a new constitution; Zhirinovsky's party surges
alternates.summary: On December 12, 1993, Russians approved a new presidential constitution and elected a new parliament, in which Vladimir Zhirinovsky's Liberal Democratic Party won the largest share of the party-list vote.
alternates.significance: The constitution entrenched Yeltsin's power after the October crisis, but the nationalist vote alarmed the West.
alternates.fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of December 13, 1993, carried Poltoranin warning Zhirinovskiy could become president in 1994, and ROSSIYSKAYA GAZETA printing the electoral commission's appeal on the constitutional vote.
